amendments.rule: The conjunction `וְ` is normally English *and*, including the waw of a consecutive verb form: the conjunction takes *And* and the verb takes the verb. Where the ASV renders it by some other connective, align it to that word instead. **The list is open and is read off the ASV rather than checked against a set**: the corpus already aligns a waw to *but*, *then*, *so*, *or*, *now*, *also*, *for*, *therefore*, *neither*, *nor*, *yea*, *yet*, *even*, *with*, *moreover* and *howbeit*, among others. A connective the ASV has written for a waw is never `added`, and it is never folded into a neighbouring word to avoid one: a town list writes *with* for the waw of `וְחַצְרֵיהֶן` → *with their villages* and *even* for the waw of `וָיָמָּה` → *even unto the sea*, and each waw takes the word written for it. **Where the ASV renders one waw by a correlative pair such as *both … and* or *either … or*, both English words belong to the waw's one discontinuous unit, headed on the closing connective (*and* or *or*); the opening correlative is not `added`.** **But that governs only a pair no other morpheme has a claim on.** Where another morpheme standing in the clause is itself what the opening correlative says — a present negative for the *neither* of *neither … nor*, the `מִן` of a `מִן … עַד` range for the *both* of *both … and* — that morpheme takes the opening word and the waw takes only the closing connective, exactly as rule 47 gives a written *the* to a present article before a supplied one and rule 46 gives a *that* to a present relative before a bare participle. `אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יָדְעוּ הֵמָּה וַאֲבוֹתָם` → *whom* ***neither*** *they* ***nor*** *their fathers have known* gives *neither* to `לֹא` and *nor* to the waw, and `מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` → ***both*** *the birds of the heavens* ***and*** *the beasts* gives *both* to `מִן` and *and* to the waw, leaving the `עַד` `unrepresented` under rule 40. Count the correlative's members against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. This does not touch rule 35's fusion, which is a single English word carrying every morpheme's sense: a lone *Nor* or *neither* with no answering *nor* written is that rule's, and only a written pair is this one's. Read what stands in the clause for that waw in particular, as rule 51 requires for *also*, and where the ASV leaves it unrendered, mark it `unrepresented`.
amendments.why: Rule 14's correlative sentence assumes the pair renders the waw alone, and JER.9 met the case it had not considered twice, from two different constructions. At 9.16 `אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יָדְעוּ הֵמָּה וַאֲבוֹתָם` → 'whom neither they nor their fathers have known' a written `לֹא` stands in the clause; read literally the rule would hand 'neither ... nor' wholly to the waw and leave that present negative unrepresented, which rule 35's 'align what is actually there' forbids. At 9.10 `מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` → 'both the birds of the heavens and the beasts' the `מִן` of the range is what the opening 'both' says. Both verses independently gave the opening word to the licensing morpheme and the closing connective to the waw, so the chapter is internally consistent and the contract sentence was the thing out of step. The qualification is not new doctrine: it is the principle the contract already states at rule 47 ('A present article morpheme takes the English the before a supplied one does') and at rule 46's first rider ('a present morpheme takes its English before a bare participle does'), applied to correlatives. It is written as a narrowing of the existing sentence rather than a new rule so that a pass reading rule 14 first is not invited into the wrong analysis, and the closing sentence protects rule 35's single-word fusions, of which this chapter has three (9.10, 9.13, 9.23) that must keep working as they do. The corpus's 19 waw units aligned to 'both and' are untouched, since they are pairs no competing morpheme has a claim on.

conventions: The formula ne'um-YHWH is aligned throughout as ne'um -> 'saith' and YHWH -> 'Jehovah' (9.3, 9.6, 9.9, 9.22, 9.24, 9.25). The ASV renders the construct noun by a finite verb, so it writes no 'of' and rule 19 has nothing to place on the divine name; the formula is not read as a construct chain in this chapter.

mi yitten is one noncompositional optative unit -> 'Oh that' in both places it stands (9.1, 9.2), headed on mi as the deterministic display anchor under rule 6 and on 'Oh' as the lexical English anchor. Where the verb carries an object suffix (9.2 yittenani), the suffix is split off and takes the ASV's recast 'I had' under rule 43's third case, so the idiom's own rendering stays identical across the two verses instead of absorbing the possessive recasting in one of them.

mibbeli is read three ways in this chapter and none of them is a split; each is what the ASV writes. 9.11 mibbeli yoshev -> 'without inhabitant' fuses the two morphemes into one English word under rule 30. 9.12 mibbeli 'over and 9.10 mibbeli ish 'over are recast as negative result clauses, so the preposition takes 'so that' under rule 48 and beli takes 'none'. In 9.10 alone, where ish is also present, beli and ish fuse into that single 'none' under rule 30, which is why 9.12's beli carries 'none' by itself.

The italic simile frame 'as it were' at 9.3 (qashtam -> 'as it were their bow') is aligned to the bare accusative of comparison rather than marked added: rule 33 gives such a noun the function word its case-function licenses, and the frame's dummy 'it were' is construction-supplied on rule 20's terms. The ASV italics corroborate only (rule 7). This is the chapter's one italic that is not `added`; 'else' (9.7), 'who is' (9.12), 'and' (9.21), 'them' (9.22), 'their' (9.25) and 'of their hair' (9.26) all are, because no morpheme licenses them.

report: Checked all 52 candidate lemma groups. Every bucket with more than one treatment is licensed either by different ASV English or by a morpheme present in one context and absent in the other; no construction in this chapter was analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference. Patches array is empty.

The three-way mibbeli family is the closest thing to a split and is not one: 9.11 mibbeli yoshev -> 'without inhabitant' fuses under rule 30 (one English word); 9.10 and 9.12 are both recast as negative result clauses, so min takes 'so that' and beli takes 'none' under rule 48; and only in 9.10, where ish is also present, do beli and ish fuse into that single 'none'. The three verse notes already cross-reference each other.

The table is blind to `added` units, so I read the dump end to end for them. All 10 are supplied English no morpheme licenses: italic 'else' (9.7), 'them' (9.22), 'their' (9.25), 'of their hair' (9.26), 'who is' (9.12); surplus connectives 'but' (9.3), 'and' (9.12, 9.21); the lexical subject 'men' (9.10); the complementizer 'that' (9.24). The mirror cases where supplied English was folded instead each have a licensor: 'the'/'a' under rule 15, copulas under rules 20 and 49, relatives and antecedents under rules 41 and 46, accusative prepositions under rule 33.

The sharpest added/folded pair is deliberate and correct: 9.8 yedabber -> 'one speaketh' keeps the indefinite subject pronoun with the verb, while 9.10 shame'u -> 'can hear' leaves 'men' added. Rule 17 draws exactly that line between a pronoun realizing the verb's person and number and a supplied lexical subject noun, and 'men' is the rule's own example.

Real cross-verse finding, and it lands on the contract rather than on the chapter: 9.16 renders lo ... waw as 'neither ... nor' and 9.10 renders min ... waw ... ad as 'both ... and'. Both verses gave the opening correlative to the morpheme that licenses it and the closing connective to the waw. The two verses agree with each other, but rule 14's correlative sentence read literally would hand the whole pair to the waw and leave a written lo unrepresented. Amendment to rule 14 returned; no verse edge changed.

BSB: none of the 14 disagreements is an error. Four object markers are rule 16's ordinary unrepresented H853; six prepositions (9.5, 9.9, 9.10, 9.11, 9.13, 9.25) are silenced by the ASV's recasting under rule 40, the 9.10 one being the ad of the 'both ... and' figure; 9.12's he is the adjective's repeated agreement article under rule 47; 9.15's two articles are unrepresented because the demonstrative zeh supplies the determination, exactly as rule 29's he'arim ha'elleh -> 'these cities'; and 9.22's waw is unrepresented because the ASV writes no connective at the head of that clause. All are documented convention differences where BSB attaches the morpheme to its phrase.

Also checked and found licensed rather than split: the three treatments of X+paneh (9.7 mippenei -> 'because of' fused, 9.13 lifnei -> 'before' fused, 9.22 al-penei split three ways because the ASV spends 'open' on penei) turn on rule 30's one-English-word condition; the article-versus-supplied-'the' split across 9.12, 9.17, 9.22, 9.23 turns on counting the ASV's 'the's per rules 29 and 47; and et takes English only at 9.1 ('for', verb-to-object preposition) and 9.15 ('even', appositional), being unrepresented in all 12 other places.

Four conventions logged. The validation report listed 47 repeated notes; the great majority are restatements of contract rules ("Noun.", "Conjunction.", "Suffix -> possessive (rule 18).") and are deliberately not logged, so that the four that carry an actual judgment are visible.
